title: Make drain work in-limit proposals and approved-work jobs
summary: Drain lists audience implementation-rung proposals as "needs a person" and ignores the Proposed job `approve-work` makes, because it only takes steward-channel Queued requests. I read the request as: drain approves open proposals whose rung the raising role may change itself, and works jobs recorded as approved by a work decision. Proposals above the limit still wait for a person. The audience is the operator running `athena drain`.

defaults_applied.how: The change is Rust in athena-cli and athena-core.
Stub-driven tests in tests/drain.rs cover both paths; clippy and fmt are clean.
Both gaps are fixed in how drain builds its queue, not by special-casing the two named items.
The limit check uses the existing may_change function, not prose.
One focused change to drain's queue and approval step.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The audience role's proposals are always rung implementation (audience.rs), so drain should compare the item's rung against the limit of the role named in WorkItem.role, using roles::may_change; a missing role definition leaves the item waiting.
Approving in drain reuses Athena::approve_work, so the request copy and decision record are unchanged; the cost of its reading counts against the budget.
Approved-work jobs have channel cli and state Proposed, so they are found through Approved work decisions, not the steward channel.
A newly approved proposal's job is worked in the same drain run, within the existing budget, retry and job-limit rules.

acceptance_criteria.text: A test in crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs gives drain an open proposal on the implementation rung from a role whose limit covers it. It shows the proposal is approved and its job is read, run and landed, and that it is not in the report's waiting list. Run `cargo test -p athena-cli --test drain`.

A test shows an open proposal above its raising role's limit (or from an unknown role) is not approved or worked by drain and still appears as waiting, with the "needs a person" text. Run `cargo test -p athena-cli --test drain`.

A test shows a job that a work decision records as approved, which is read but not yet run (state proposed), is picked up and run by drain once. A job already closed is not picked up again. Run `cargo test -p athena-cli --test drain`.

The module text in drain.rs no longer says drain has no way to approve a proposal. It states that in-limit proposals are approved and approved jobs are worked. Rejecting, and approving above-limit proposals, stay with people.

out_of_scope: Changing the ladder rules in roles.rs or the top-two-rungs restriction
Auto-approving proposals above a role's limit
departures: The change touches drain's Steps trait, the queue model and tests, and needs a lookup of roles. That is larger than the typical job, so I raised cost and time above the reference and lowered the pass probability.
